title: Payaquotusk (Pipe's Neck)
summary: Payaquotusk is a Southold placename for Pipe's Neck in the Arshamomaque and Hashamomuk Neck landscape.
map_geometry_source: Approximate modern Pipe's Neck point based on Tooker location; not an exact historical neck boundary. Offset slightly from nearby Manhansuck/Pipe's Neck Creek marker for map visibility.
introduction_content: Payaquotusk is identified as the neck northeast of William Salmon's house on Hashamomuk Neck, now known as Pipe's Neck.
history_content: The placename belongs to the Arshamomaque and Hashamomuk Neck landscape west of Greenport. Boundary and Paucamp context appear in the historic moments below.
translation_content:
The name is connected with the estuary at the southern end of the neck, where the water divides into two branches. The history cross-references Paucuckatux, a related divided-creek placename.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names are wayfinders and memory-aides. People need them to communicate shared knowledge of places and how to get to them.”

— Dyarubbin project team, Why Are Place Names Important? (2024), About page, ‘Why Are Place Names Important?’
whereintheworld_content: Approximate/general point on Pipe's Neck west of Greenport in Southold. This marker is not an exact historical neck boundary or estuary-branch coordinate.
